# Reproduction table — Stage 1 (DRAFT, generated by scripts/stage1_gates.py)

LLaMA2-7B (Meta weights, **8-bit group-64 MLX**), PromptEOL, view `fwd`, `<PST>` row seed 3407, Spearman x100,
STS12-16 pooled ("all"). r1 = layer 32 after the final norm, r2 = layer 27 (both vanilla, batch 1, one pass),
r3 = TP s=1 e=7 (e* chosen on dev) layer 27, r3' = TP s=1 e=8 layer 27 (both equal-length batched, validated in S0.13).
Test: 18,850 pairs / 28,530 unique sentences. Comparisons with the paper are descriptive (different stack; no bootstrap).

## Precision note (S1.5 replacement; STS-B dev, layer 27 unless stated)

| Model | r1_dev (L32 normed) | r2_dev (L27) | r3_dev (TP e=7) | TP gain (dev) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Meta 4-bit group 64 | 73.41 | 78.84 | 81.69 | +2.85 |
| **Meta 8-bit group 64 (main)** | 74.13 | 79.72 | 82.44 | +2.73 |

Why 8-bit is the main model: both 4-bit group-64 conversions (third-party and our own from Meta weights) put
`▁Unterscheidung` as the top next token after a full stop with P(newline) = 0 and drift into German in greedy
continuations (5/5 prompts); 8-bit shows neither (0/5) and scores 0.7-0.9 points higher on dev while leaving the TP
gain essentially unchanged. No fp16 reference was run on this Mac, so the 8-bit quantisation effect itself is not
isolated. Details: notes/decisions.md, logs/diag_*.json, logs/devcheck_meta*.json.

## Timing (S1.8, batch 1 for both, 200 dev sentences, 20 warm-up, 3 repeats, M = 27)

Vanilla 154.1 ± 0.3 ms/sentence, TP e=7 158.2 ± 0.5 ms/sentence,
ratio **1.026x** (paper 1.04x with KV cache on STS-B test; ours has no KV cache, one forward per sentence, and stops after layer 27).
Mean prompt length 28.1 vs 29.1 tokens (TP adds the `<PST>` token).
